newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga shuts in Snorre due power failure.
newsitem.headline: Saga shuts in Snorre due power failure.

text.p: Saga Petroleum said on Monday production at the 200,000 barrels per day Snorre oil field had been shut in because of a power failure and that it may resume on Tuesday at the earliest.
"Oil production at Snorre stopped yesterday at 9 p.m. (1900 GMT) because of a short circuit in the electricity when we were testing an oil export pump," Saga spokesman Bjoern Schiebevaag said.
"It shut down the main electricity supply on the platform. We are now running on an auxiliary generator," he told Reuters.

"The production was immediately stopped and the wells were secured. We are working to get the main electricity up again. This can happen tonight at the earliest. The earliest we can resume oil production is tomorrow," Schiebevaag told Reuters.
The North Sea field pumped 192,688 bpd in June.
